title: Dress well for prayer. Eat and drink, without excess.
subtitle: Beauty at the masjid, balance at the table
then: This answered the practice of going around the Ka'bah naked. Allah told people to {idea}take their adornment to every masjid{/idea}. Ibn Abbas said: {reward}eat and wear what you wish{/reward}, as long as you avoid two things, {trap}extravagance and arrogance{/trap}.
now: You throw on the gym hoodie for prayer, but you dress up for a dinner with friends. At that dinner you order three dishes and take half home to forget in the fridge. {idea}The verse flips both habits.{/idea}
old: Prayer clothes do not matter, and food is mine to waste.
new: I bring my best to Allah and stop at enough at the table.
try: Wear something clean and nice for your next prayer, and stop one meal before you are full.

title: Who forbade the good things Allah made for you?
subtitle: Beauty and good food are His gifts
then: The idolaters had banned certain foods and clothes {trap}from their own opinions, with no basis from Allah{/trap}. The verse asks who gave them that right. The tafsir says these gifts are {reward}for believers in this life, and only theirs in the next{/reward}.
now: Someone in your circle says wearing nice things or enjoying a good meal is not for real believers. You start feeling guilty over a new coat. {idea}Allah made beautiful things for His servants. Guilt was not part of the gift.{/idea}
old: Enjoying nice things must make me less religious.
new: Good things are Allah's gifts to His servants, meant to be enjoyed with thanks.
try: Enjoy one good thing today fully, and say alhamdulillah out loud for it.

title: What He really forbade is a short, serious list.
subtitle: Five things my Lord prohibited
then: After asking who forbade good things, the verse says what Allah did forbid. The Prophet ﷺ said {idea}none is more protective than Allah{/idea}, which is why He forbade indecency, open or secret. Mujahid and others explained that {trap}sin harms yourself, oppression harms others{/trap}, and both are forbidden.
now: You argue online for an hour about which clothes are allowed. The same evening you snap at your sibling and forward a rumor about a coworker. {idea}The serious list was about the second part of your day.{/idea}
old: Religion is mostly about the small details of dress and food.
new: Allah's real lines are around harm, injustice, shirk and lies about Him.
try: Check today for one of these five in your own day: hidden sin, unfairness, or speaking about Allah without knowing.

title: Every people has a deadline. Not one hour early or late.
subtitle: A set term no one can move
then: The tafsir says every {idea}generation and nation has its appointed term{/idea}, which it was destined for. When it comes, {trap}they cannot delay it or bring it forward{/trap}, not even by an hour.
now: The calendar on your phone is full of plans for next year. None of them knows your real deadline. {idea}Neither does any doctor in any hospital corridor.{/idea} {trap}It will not move for unfinished business.{/trap}
old: I can always put off the important things for a while.
new: My term is fixed, so what I mean to do for Allah should not wait.
try: Do the one thing you would regret leaving undone, or start it, today.

title: Messengers came. Fear Allah, fix things, and fear nothing.
subtitle: No fear and no grief for the careful

row.title: taqwa and reform
sub: leave the bad, do the good

then: Right after the deadline, Allah reminds the children of Adam that He sent messengers with good news and warning. The tafsir explains taqwa and reform as {idea}leaving what is forbidden and doing what He asks{/idea}. For them: {reward}no fear and no grief{/reward}.
now: You lie awake doing the math on the mortgage, your kid's grades, your health check. {reward}The verse offers a quieter way to sleep{/reward}: be careful with Allah, and fix what is in your hands.
old: I will feel safe once everything in life is under control.
new: Real safety comes from taqwa and fixing what I can.
try: Fix one thing you have let slide, a debt, an apology, a prayer, today.

title: Denying the signs out of pride has a lasting cost.
subtitle: The other side of the same choice
then: Next to the promise of the last verse comes its opposite. The tafsir says {trap}their hearts denied the signs, and they were too arrogant to follow them{/trap}. The two paths are set side by side so the listener can choose.
now: Sometimes it is not that you do not know. You know prayer is due; you know the lie was wrong. {trap}What stops you is that changing feels like losing.{/trap} {idea}Notice that pride, and the door is still open.{/idea}
old: I would follow if the truth were only clearer.
new: Often the truth is clear and pride is what holds me back.
try: Do one good thing today that your pride has been resisting.

title: At death they ask: where are your helpers now?
subtitle: Every false support disappears at the end
then: Those who lie about Allah still get {reward}their share of provision and life{/reward}, the tafsir says, until death comes. Then the angels ask where the others they invoked have gone. They answer: {trap}they have vanished and deserted us{/trap}, and confess against themselves.
now: The boss you flatter, the connections, the savings, the lucky ritual you do before exams. {trap}All of it leaves the room at the end.{/trap} {idea}Ask now what you would answer if asked where they are.{/idea}
old: The people and things I rely on will carry me through.
new: Only Allah remains when every other support leaves.
try: Name one thing you lean on more than Allah, and give it back to its proper size today.

title: The followers blame their leaders. Each gets double.
subtitle: Blame does not lighten anyone's load
then: Each group that enters curses the one before it. The followers ask that their leaders get double, because {trap}these misled us{/trap}. The answer is that {idea}each one has double{/idea}, recompensed by their own deeds. The tafsir links it to verses where leaders and followers disown each other.
now: "Everyone in the office was doing it." "My friends pushed me." {trap}The blame feels like a shield.{/trap} {idea}The verse says it lightens no one: the one who led and the one who followed both carry their part.{/idea}
old: If someone else led me into it, it is mostly their fault.
new: Blaming the one who led me does not remove my own share.
try: Take ownership out loud of one thing you have been blaming on someone else.

title: You were no better than us, the leaders reply.
subtitle: No one is spared by pointing fingers
then: The leaders answer the followers' complaint. As-Suddi explained it as {trap}you were led astray as we were led astray{/trap}. Then comes the line: {idea}taste it for what you used to earn{/idea}.
now: The group chat that mocked someone. You did not start it; you only added the laughing emoji. {idea}Following is still a choice you made with your own thumb.{/idea}
old: Going along with the crowd makes me less responsible.
new: Following someone into wrong is still my own choice and my own earning.
try: The next time a group goes somewhere wrong today, stay quiet or walk away instead of joining.

title: A camel through a needle's eye. That closed a door.
subtitle: When pride shuts the gates of heaven

row.title: gates of heaven
sub: deeds and duas do not rise

then: Ibn Abbas and others said the gates not opening means {trap}their good deeds and duas will not rise{/trap}. Others said it refers to their souls; Ibn Jurayj combined both. The image of a camel through a needle's eye shows {idea}how impossible it is while the pride remains{/idea}.
now: You make dua, but never let go of the thing you know is wrong and refuse to admit. {idea}The verse is not about strangers. It asks whether your own pride is blocking your own door.{/idea}
old: My duas go up no matter how I treat Allah's signs.
new: Pride toward the truth can block the very door my duas go through.
try: Before your next dua, admit to Allah one thing you have been too proud to admit.

title: A bed beneath and coverings above, of fire.
subtitle: The recompense of the wrongdoers
then: Al-Qurazi explained the words as {trap}beds below and coverings over them{/trap}, from the Fire. The verse closes with {idea}thus do We recompense the wrongdoers{/idea}, after describing those who denied the signs with pride.
now: Tonight you will pull the blanket up and scroll before sleep. {idea}A warm bed is a mercy you did not earn.{/idea} {reward}It is also a good place to think about how you want to rest later.{/reward}
old: Comfort now means I am fine.
new: The rest I get later depends on what I do with my days now.
try: Before sleeping tonight, think over your day for one minute and seek forgiveness for one thing.

title: Believe, do good, and you are never asked too much.
subtitle: Paradise, within your capacity
then: After the warnings, the surah turns to the happy ones. The tafsir notes that in the middle of this promise Allah says {reward}He burdens no soul beyond its scope{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says this shows {idea}that faith and acting on it are made easy{/idea}.
now: You look at people who pray the night and fast every Monday, and you think there is no point in starting. {reward}Allah never asked for their capacity. He asked for yours.{/reward}
old: If I cannot do it all, I should not bother trying.
new: Allah asks only what I can carry, and that is enough to start.
try: Pick one good deed small enough that you can do it daily this week, and do it today.

title: Every grudge removed, and they praise the One who guided.
subtitle: Paradise begins with clean hearts
then: The Prophet ﷺ said believers will be held at a bridge until {trap}wrongs between them are settled{/trap}, then enter Paradise. They praise Allah for guiding them. He ﷺ also said {reward}no one's deeds alone admit him, not even his own, unless Allah covers him with mercy{/reward}.
now: The cousin you have not spoken to since the inheritance fight. The friend who never paid you back. {idea}In Paradise, that weight is lifted off the chest.{/idea} You could start putting it down now.
old: Some grudges I will carry forever.
new: Paradise has no room for resentment, so letting go starts here.
try: Pray for one person you hold a grudge against, by name, today.

title: We found His promise true. Did you find yours?
subtitle: One question across the divide
then: The people of Paradise call across: {reward}we found our Lord's promise true{/reward}. Have you? They answer {trap}yes{/trap}. The tafsir recalls that after Badr, the Prophet ﷺ called the fallen leaders of Quraysh by name with the same question.
now: You hear about the Day and file it under "probably." You make plans for the weekend with far more certainty. {idea}One day everyone will say yes to this question. The difference is only when.{/idea}
old: The promises about the Hereafter are probably true, someday.
new: Every promise and warning from Allah will be found exactly true.
try: Read one verse about Paradise today and let yourself believe it fully for a minute.

title: They blocked the path and made it look crooked.
subtitle: Turning others away from Allah's way
then: The tafsir says they {trap}hindered people from Allah's path and made it appear crooked and winding{/trap}, so no one would follow. They denied the meeting with Allah, so {idea}they took evil words and deeds lightly{/idea}.
now: Your friend tries to start praying, and you joke that it will not last. Your sister wears hijab for the first time, and you roll your eyes. {idea}Small comments can make the straight path look crooked to someone.{/idea}
old: My little jokes about someone's faith are harmless.
new: My words can make Allah's path look easier or harder for others.
try: Encourage one person today who is trying to come closer to Allah.
